name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud

pages.text:
Strict Client Auth is a highly recommended setting for private clients, which requires all `/login` and `/authorize` requests to pass their credentials directly in the `x-slas-client-auth` header. This feature is part of a broader set of protections to help keep authentication endpoints secure and resilient against automated threats. Public clients don’t support Strict Client Auth and ignore the `x-slas-client-auth` header if present.

As a best practice and to maximize security, send both `login_id` and `channel_id` on `POST /oauth2/passwordless/token` when you exchange a passwordless one-time password for an access token. Set `login_id` to the same value as the login identifier sent when the one-time password was requested (`user_id` on `POST /oauth2/passwordless/login`, or `login_id` when registering a customer). Don’t change spelling or capitalization. Set `channel_id` to the same site sent when the one-time password was requested. PWA Kit 3.22.0 or later and Storefront Next 1.5.0 or later send both values. If you upgraded only some storefront packages or customized the passwordless login pages, see Troubleshoot Passwordless Login for PWA Kit or Troubleshoot Passwordless Login for Storefront Next.

Leaked Credentials Detection applies to `POST /shopper/auth/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/oauth2/login` because SLAS submits shopper credentials as HTTP Basic in the `Authorization` header. For a leaked-credentials match, use a SCAPI-zone rate-limiting rule with the `block` action (HTTP 429). Start the rule with the `log` action, review the matches, and then switch to `block`. Don’t use a `managed_challenge`, `js_challenge`, or `legacy_captcha` action. For storefront form login and rule examples, see Bot Management. For leaked-credentials detection and SCAPI-zone availability controls, see Security.

To protect against refresh-token replay abuse, SLAS limits how frequently a single refresh token can be exchanged at `/oauth2/token`.

Prevent guest order data from appearing in a shopper’s registered account by rotating the guest session immediately after receiving a guest order. Treat every completed guest order as a session boundary. In the recommended flow, after order confirmation, request a fresh guest token from SLAS using `grant_type=client_credentials`. Then, replace the currently stored access token and refresh token with the new ones.

Use a headless API to build custom apps. B2C Commerce API is also known as Salesforce Commerce API (SCAPI). Applies to: Composable, hybrid, and custom.

### Script API (B2C Commerce Developer Resources)

Access B2C Commerce data (such as product and shopper data) and functionality (such as baskets and orders) through secure and well-defined API methods. Applies to: Composable, SFRA, hybrid, and custom.

Access developer guides and API reference documentation for Point of Sale.

* Functional scopes (`c_` prefix): These custom scopes authorize the execution of your specific business logic. They handle the request authorization for the code itself.
* Diagnostic/Administrative Scope (`sfcc.custom-apis` and `sfcc.custom-apis.rw`): This scope is required to access the DX API. While your `c_` scope runs your custom code, the `sfcc.custom-apis` scope provides the necessary visibility into the registration status and scaffolding of the Custom API framework.

Custom APIs must be secured by a security scheme which includes exactly one functional scope. Custom API clients must obtain a token with the required scope. To secure your custom endpoints and make authorized requests to them, complete the following steps:

1. Choose a security scheme and custom scope for the endpoint.
2. Update your API client to include the custom scope in tokens.

The Custom APIs DX endpoint uses an Account Manager OAuth 2.0 bearer token for authentication and you must specify one of the following scopes to access this API endpoint:

* `ShopperToken`: For Shopper APIs and storefront use cases. Use Shopper Login and API Access to obtain tokens.
* `AmOAuth2`: For SCAPI Admin APIs to be used with backoffice apps. Use Account Manager to obtain tokens.

This topic is for **ISVs** who want merchants to discover and install the app from Business Manager. Submit your Commerce App to the registry for review and publication.

1. Ensure `b2c cap validate` passes with no errors
2. Produce your final `.zip` via `b2c cap package`
3. Issue a Pull Request against the Commerce App Registry to submit the package along with required metadata (app name, version, description, supported platform versions, documentation)
4. The review team will evaluate your submission and collaborate with your team against your PR before approving.

**Draft:** Initial submission received, not yet in review.

**In Review:** The review team is evaluating your app.

**Approved:** Your app is approved and published to the registry.

You research apps for an agent-toolkit builder. App: Salesforce Commerce Cloud (category: Ecommerce; hint: developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce).
Using ONLY the SOURCES below, fill the schema. Rules:
- access: can a developer get credentials themselves for free (self_serve_free), only on a paid plan/trial, only after app review/approval, or only via partnership/contact sales?
- buildability: could this be an agent toolkit today (yes / yes_with_caveats / no); blocker = main obstacle, else "none".
- existing_mcp only if SOURCES show it; otherwise none_found (or unknown if sources are silent).
- evidence: for each of auth_methods, access, api_types, existing_mcp give a url from SOURCES and a SHORT VERBATIM quote (<=200 chars) copied exactly from that source's text. No quote available -> say unknown, do not invent.
- If sources are insufficient, use "unknown". Never guess from memory.
